title: How an Optical Mouse Works in 60 Seconds 🖱️📸 #shorts
description:
An optical mouse is really a tiny high-speed camera. An LED lights up the desk at a low angle, a small image sensor snaps over a thousand pictures of the surface texture every second, and a processor compares each frame with the last to work out how far and in which direction you moved. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#mouse #computer #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An optical mouse snaps over a *thousand* pictures of your desk every second.

steps.label: LED
steps.text: Underneath, a red *LED* shines across the desk at a *low angle*, so tiny bumps cast shadows.

steps.label: Camera
steps.text: A tiny *camera sensor* behind a lens captures those bumps and the *texture* of the surface.

steps.label: Compare
steps.text: A built in *processor* compares each picture with the *last one*.

steps.label: Motion
steps.text: From how the texture *shifted*, it works out the *direction* and distance you moved.

steps.label: Cursor
steps.text: Those moves are sent to the computer, and your *cursor* glides across the screen to match.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Light, snap, *compare*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
